newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks curb losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks curb losses at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks took a fresh hit Monday but pared losses at the close as volume petered out and were seen fairly steady, dealers said.

"The market found support and clawed back a bit, imitating movements on Wall Street," said trader Rodrigo Diz at Velox Inversiones. "I expect we'll see a trading lull before the Federal Reserve meeting (March 25), with prices weak but more or less trapped within these ranges."
The blue-chip .MERV index dropped 1.3 percent to a five-week low of 702.45. It fell 2.6 percent last week and stands 2.1 percent lower so far in March.
The MerVal had slipped as low as 696 in the session and technical analysts predicted it would not fall below 690 in the near term.

"It's very encouraging that the MerVal pierced 700 with little volume on the trading floor, because that tends to show there's limited downside," another trader said. "However, we remain very conditioned by the Wall Street factor."
Floor turnover eased to 15 million pesos from an already paltry tally of 16.9 million Friday, while over-the-counter deals picked up to 156.2 million pesos from 104.9 million Friday.
The broad market index also recouped some losses to close off 1.4 percent, with losing issues thrashing winners 42 to five and 11 stocks closing flat.
Heaviest main-tier losses were run up by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which fell 3.2 percent, and Telefonica and Telecom, which pulled back 2.9 and 2.5 percent, respectively.
The only MerVal risers were steelmaker Siderar and holding company Comercial del Plata, which gained 2.4 percent and 0.3 percent, respectively.
